_comment: Single source of truth for jobpipe v2 and the unified daily run. SKILL.md and references/*.md describe these rules in words; change the rule here and the words there together, then run the tests.

profile._comment: Years by function (SKILL.md experience table). The years gate compares a posting's required years with the row its wording points to, never the ~6-year total.

skills._comment: From resumes/*.md only. strong = shown in work or projects; some = coursework / lighter use. Used for the skills pre-score; Claude re-checks against the resume when scoring.

graduation._note: Roles limited to 'Class of 2027' / graduating after Dec 2026 may not accept a May 2026 graduate: flag, don't drop.

sectors._comment: Eight sectors. 'startups' is not a row value: it is every company with startup=yes, whatever its industry. Sector labels a role; it never limits a query.

professional._finance_analytics_note: Added Oct 28 2026: she applied to Sr. Financial Analyst, Senior Analyst Pricing & Monetization, MSR Hedging Analyst and similar roles, and financial modeling is her longest function row (~4 yrs). Remove the group to stop searching it.

newgrad._comment: New-grad program roles for SDE / MLE / AI (+ FDE and quant). A title must carry a new-grad marker, or come from a new-grad list (SimplifyJobs, speedyapply, CareerBuzz, Interstride entry-level filter).

query_families._comment: What every general website is searched for. 'or' is one boolean query for sites that accept OR (LinkedIn, Indeed); 'each' are short queries for sites that need them (2-3 words). Every family is searched on every site whose 'programs' include it, unless the site lists 'families'.

data_analytics.or: "data analyst" OR "analytics engineer" OR "business intelligence" OR "AI operations analyst"

ml_ai_engineering.or: "machine learning engineer" OR "AI engineer" OR "applied AI" OR "member of technical staff"

consulting_strategy.or: "data consultant" OR "analytics consultant" OR "AI consultant" OR "strategy & analytics" OR bizops

risk_quant.or: "quantitative analyst" OR "model validation" OR "model risk" OR "credit risk" OR "risk analytics" OR "fraud data scientist"

finance_analytics.or: "financial analyst" OR "investment analyst" OR "FP&A" OR "pricing analyst" OR "real estate analyst"

sde.or: "new grad" software engineer OR "software engineer I" OR "entry level software engineer"

mle.or: "new grad" "machine learning" OR "machine learning engineer I" OR "entry level machine learning"

ai.or: "new grad" "AI engineer" OR "entry level AI engineer" OR "AI engineer I"

quant_fde.or: "new grad" quantitative OR "quant researcher" OR "new grad" "forward deployed"

sites.name: Google Jobs

The date chip is set by htichips (today / 3days / week); if the URL form changes, open google.com/search?q=<query>+jobs, click 'Jobs' and set 'Date posted'. A consent page or CAPTCHA is a valid blocker.

gates.senior_eng_note: 'Senior Applied AI Engineer I' (Juniper Square) was applied to: titles ending in level I pass the senior-engineering gate and go to the years check.
gates.level_exclude_note: Calibrated on her Oct 24-28 decisions: she applied to Data Scientist III, MLE II, Senior Data Scientist, Sr. Quantitative Finance Analyst and Senior Analyst roles, and skipped Sr MLE, Sr Data Engineer, BIE II (SQL/ETL engineering), MLE 4 and Manager titles. So engineering III+ and senior-engineering titles are gated; Senior Associate / Senior Analyst / Senior Consultant / Senior Data Scientist / Scientist III are scored, not gated.

years_gate._comment: Hard exclusion only where her decisions show it: engineering and people-management years. Other functions lose experience points instead (score, not gate).
years_gate._soft_points_note: [gap_years, points]: gap = asked - has(function row). gap <= 0 -> 20, <= 1 -> 16, <= 3 -> 10 (Stretch flag), more -> 4 ('large years gap' flag). Asks < 2 years -> 20 in any function.

no_sponsorship: (?<!with or )without (?:the need for |requiring )?(?:current or future |now or in the future |future )?(?:any |the |an? )?(?:(?:employment|visa|work|immigration|h-?1-?b|employer|employment visa|work visa)[ -])*sponsorship
must be (?:legally )?authorized to work in the (?:u\.?s\.?|united states) without
not considering candidates who (?:will )?(?:now or in the future )?require (?:any |the |an? )?(?:(?:employment|visa|work|immigration|h-?1-?b|employer|employment visa|work visa)[ -])*sponsorship
clearance: must (?:have|hold|obtain|be able to obtain) (?:an? )?(?:active )?(?:secret|top secret|security) clearance

gates.newgrad_exclude_title_note: Word-bounded regexes (Oct 28: 'sr.' matched 'ISRT', 'intern' matched 'Internal'). Level ranges that start at 1/I ('Level 1, 2, or 3') pass.

rubric._comment: Out of 100. Gates first (a gated role is never scored). Add to a tracker at score >= add_threshold. Python pre-scores every role; Claude scores those with pre_score >= claude_threshold and re-checks skills/responsibilities on the posting.
rubric._slots: The five slots match the dashboard's score breakdown (skills_pts, experience_pts, responsibility_pts, qualifications_pts, preferences_pts); new rows also carry score_max so the page can show the new maxima.

minimums_legacy._note: Old per-run query minimums, kept only so `audit --legacy` still reads old source logs. The unified run uses the ledger (every planned item done or blocked).

jd_match._comment: Resume <-> job-description matching (jobpipe.jdmatch). What she HAS is read from resumes/*.md, never from this file. A posting's asks are the lexicon terms found in its text; asks inside requirement lines count double. skills_pts = 30 * (floor + span * match).

feed_search._comment: Search terms for employer ATS that need a query (Workday, Oracle). Broad on purpose: titles are screened afterwards. Workday is paged to the end of each query, up to workday_max_pages x 20 postings.

sponsors._comment: DOL LCA disclosure data (H-1B), built by `sponsors-build`, used for (a) sponsorship evidence in the score and (b) growing companies.csv (`registry-grow`). Files: https://www.dol.gov/sites/dolgov/files/ETA/oflc/pdfs/LCA_Disclosure_Data_FY{fy}_Q{q}.xlsx (quarterly, cumulative within the fiscal year; FY starts Oct 1).

discovery._comment: Discovery finds companies the registry does not have yet. A card at a company already in companies.csv is dropped on sight (that company is harvested directly); a good card at an unknown company is pursued, and when its role is added to a tracker the company is added to the registry (registry_additions.csv).
